condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

L4 intestinal-absorption records show complete or near-complete human absorption for related small lipophilic drugs, including phenylbutazone (C57), diazepam (C51, C59, C61), and ketoprofen (C52, C55, C58, C60, C62); phenylbutazone shares the pyrazolone/pyrazolidinedione core.

L5 gut-wall records show very high permeability for edaravone (C72), a closely related pyrazolone, and high Papp with efflux ratios near 1 for other small heterocycles (C68, C64, C66, C67, C73, C71), indicating no gut-wall efflux barrier.
